t.7.83.1: Having swiftly dispatched all of that in its entirety, the elder brother of Bharata released the horse, dappled black and endowed with auspicious marks.
t.7.83.2: Having appointed Lakṣmaṇa, together with the priests, to the horse, Kākutstha then went with his army to Naimiṣa.
t.7.83.4: While he was dwelling in Naimiṣa, all the kings came from every kingdom, and Rāma honored them in return.
t.7.83.3: Seeing the supremely wondrous sacrificial enclosure, the glorious, mighty-armed one felt incomparable joy, and he spoke thus.
t.7.83.6: Then Bharata, accompanied by Śatrughna, quickly provided food, drink and garments to those great-souled ones together with their followers.
t.7.83.5: And the greatly radiant best of men assigned costly lodgings to the great-souled kings and their followers.
t.7.83.7: And then the great-souled monkeys, together with Sugrīva, all bowing humbly, served food to the Brāhmaṇas.
t.7.83.8: And Vibhīṣaṇa, surrounded by many garlanded Rākṣasas, stood in attendance as a servant upon the sages of fierce austerities.
t.7.83.9: Thus the well-ordered sacrifice, the horse-sacrifice, proceeded, and the wandering of the horse, guarded by Lakṣmaṇa, was set in motion.
t.7.83.10: At the horse sacrifice of the great-souled one no other sound was heard there but this: “Give freely and without hesitation, as long as the petitioners remain unsatisfied!” And just so much was seen being given by the vānaras and rākṣasas.
t.7.83.11: At that excellent sacrifice of the king, thronged with joyful and well-nourished people, no one there was soiled, nor wretched, nor emaciated.
t.7.83.12: And the great-souled, long-lived sages who were present there could not recall any sacrifice like it, adorned with such floods of gifts.
t.7.83.13: Of the silver, gold, jewels and garments being given away without ceasing, no end was to be seen.
t.7.83.15: Everywhere stood the monkeys, and everywhere too the Rākṣasas; with full hands they gave clothing and riches abundantly to all who desired them.
t.7.83.14: "Neither of Śakra nor of Soma, nor of Yama or Varuṇa, has such a one ever been seen by us before," thus spoke the ascetics.
t.7.83.16: Such was the sacrifice of that lion among kings, endowed with every excellence; it went on for a full year and more, and in no way did it diminish.
